scenario.name: Dragos FrostyGoop Report, CERT-UA & CISA ICS — Industrial ENCO Controller Modbus TCP Port 502 Register Audit
scenario.overview: Picture a bustling restaurant kitchen with a stainless-steel pass-through counter, a hanging rail of paper order tickets, a glowing drive-thru window, and a line chef at the stove. Pulling up to the restaurant drive-thru window, a clever customer asks for a routine meal while sneaking an extra kitchen command onto the special-notes line of the order. In this real-world scenario, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the line chef's station, then smuggles copied records out past the drive-thru order window in tiny disguised batches. The restaurant manager inspects the kitchen receipt printer tape and spots an impossible order note that gave away stock without a matching sale. In this scenario (T1190, Dragos FrostyGoop Report, CERT-UA & CISA ICS, Industrial ENCO Controller Modbus TCP Port 502 Register Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: external Modbus TCP Port 502 Session, then bulk Holding Register Enumeration, then holding Register Overwrite via Function. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering External Modbus TCP Port 502 Session, then Bulk Holding Register Enumeration, then Holding Register Overwrite via Function, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on Zeek Event 502 correlated across the documented kill chain.

steps.storyAnalogy: Instead of serving only the paid sandwich, the kitchen passes the back-office recipe binder and extra stock straight out through the pickup window. steps.simpleExplanation: Zeek ICS logs capture Function Code 0x06 (Write Single Register) and Function Code 0x10 (Write Multiple Registers) modifying heating controller parameters and inaccurate temperature calibration offsets, prompting OT incident responders to verify controller register state from engineering backups (logged in Zeek ICS Event 16 with ModbusFunction=0x10 , Write Multiple Registers, ModifiedAddresses=Registers 40101–40108 , Valve Actuator & Thermal Setpoint, DetectionAlert=SURICATA Modbus Unauthorized Write Multiple Registers from External Subnet so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
